swamp noun

also marsh, bog, fen, marshland, mire, marshes

classical

Traupman 206

palūs, palūdis f.

noun, third declension

swamp, marsh

Other words

  • ūlīgō, ūlīginis f. — the wetness of the ground; boggy soil

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Varr. RR 2.2.7 (Lewis & Short); Verg. G. 2.184 (Lewis & Short); Tac. Ann. 1.64 (Lewis & Short)

  • lāma, lāmae f. — a slough, a bog

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Hor. Ep. 1.13.10: per clīvōs, flūmina, lāmās (Lewis & Short)

    A rare word; Festus explains it as a gathering of water, a lacūna (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • quamvīs lapis omnia nūdus līmōsōque palūs obdūcat pāscua juncō

    though bare stone and marsh with its muddy rushes cover all the pasturesVerg. E. 1.47–48

See also reed, rush, sedge, alder, pond, mud, lake, marshy.
